title: Flap Carriage Roller and Outboard Track Wear Standard Change
abstract: Change of the outboard flap carriage roller material and of the track wear limits, following accelerated wear on high-cycle aircraft that was consuming the whole life of the track between heavy checks.

sections.reason: Wear measurements at the outboard carriage on high-cycle aircraft showed the track reaching its published limit at about nineteen thousand flight cycles rather than the thirty-two thousand assumed in the maintenance programme. Fourteen tracks were replaced early across the fleet in two years and two of those were found at the limit at an intermediate check, which meant an aircraft flying with a track outside limits for an unknown period. The mechanism was traced to the roller surface hardness relative to the track, which put the wear into the track rather than into the roller as designed.
sections.description: The outboard carriage roller is changed to a softer surface treatment so that wear is taken by the roller, which is a replaceable item, rather than by the track, which is not. The carriage actuator assembly DEL97190-24 is re-issued with the new roller set, the flap drive solenoid assembly D2750116570759 is unchanged but re-shimmed at the carriage interface, and the clamp sub-assembly D2750008046179 is replaced. Washers AES606871-9E are renewed at the carriage pivot and the actuator sub-assembly D2750008004169 is re-rigged after installation. The track wear limits published in the maintenance manual are revised in the same change, with a measurement method that can be done with the flap extended rather than removed. Functional item 424EV5 is affected. Work is at the flap areas in zones 561, 563 and 661. Installation detail is on drawing D27501162228.
sections.effects: Mass change is negligible. No electrical load change. The roller set is interchangeable with the earlier set and may be mixed between carriages, but not within one carriage. The wear inspection interval extends from four thousand to eight thousand flight cycles once the new roller is fitted at both outboard positions, and the measurement is now possible at a line stop, which removes the main reason operators had been deferring it. The repair manual entry for a worn track is superseded because the allowable wear figure changes.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN C00750 in March 2025. The retrofit was first offered as Service Bulletin CRN-27-2003, which was cancelled after an error in the rigging values was found during the first embodiments, and is now covered by CRN-27-2012. Six hours per side with the flap extended and supported.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00750, roller set supplied with the carriage as an assembly
